question.text: A group 13 element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi></msup></math> reacts with chlorine gas to produce a compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>XCl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi>XCl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> is electron deficient and easily reacts with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>to</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>form</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi>Cl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>←</mo><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> adduct; however, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>XCl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> does not dimerize. X is:

solution.text:
BCl3


 

Boron react with chlorine gas to produce compound BCl3 which is electron deficient. It does not dimerize because of small boron atom. It react with ammonia to form aduct. In it ammonia act as lewis base and BCl3 act as lewis acid.
